title: What are you doing this week?
content_html:
I'm currently adding multi-thread support for Argon2 in Monocypher. Without depending on any multi-thread API at all. I'm sticking to the "pure portable C99 with zero dependency" that makes this little library so easy to integrate pretty much everywhere.

Instead I chopped up the API into an init() update() final() structure that let users implement parallelism however they want:

void crypto_argon2_init(crypto_argon2_ctx *ctx, uint32_t hash_size,
                        void *work_area,
                        crypto_argon2_config config,
                        crypto_argon2_inputs inputs,
                        crypto_argon2_extras extras);
void crypto_argon2_segment(const crypto_argon2_ctx *ctx,
                           uint32_t pass, uint32_t slice, uint32_t lane);
void crypto_argon2_final(const crypto_argon2_ctx *ctx, uint8_t *hash);

The single thread implementation goes like this:

void crypto_argon2(u8 *hash, u32 hash_size, void *work_area,
                   crypto_argon2_config config,
                   crypto_argon2_inputs inputs,
                   crypto_argon2_extras extras)
{
	crypto_argon2_ctx ctx;
	crypto_argon2_init(&ctx, hash_size, work_area, config, inputs, extras);

	for (u32 pass = 0; pass < config.nb_passes; pass++) {
		for (u32, slice, 0, 4) {
			// May be done in parallel, one thread per lane.
			for (u32 lane = 0; lane < config.nb_lanes; lane++) {
				crypto_argon2_segment(&ctx, pass, slice, lane);
			}
			// Sync point: wait for all lanes to complete.
		}
	}

	crypto_argon2_final(&ctx, hash);
}

Early experiments with pthreads suggest this should easily accommodate any multi-thread API.

Next step is documentation, and provide a production worthy code example.
